question: whats the last day i can drop a class without it showing up on my transcript
notes: Fall 2026: Oct 4, 2026 (11:55 pm PT) is the last day to drop with a 100% refund; a class dropped by the deadline is removed and does not appear on the transcript. After that it is a withdrawal (W).

question: Is it too late to pick up another class this term?
notes: Fall 2026: add online without department approval through Oct 4; with department approval (an override) through Oct 11, 2026. After week 2 it takes a Petition for Late Change of Registration.

question: How long do I have to swap classes at the start of winter quarter?
notes: Winter 2027: last day to add online without dept. approval and last day to drop with a 100% refund are both Sunday, Jan 10, 2027 (classes begin Jan 4).

question: When's the cutoff to get all my money back if I bail on a course?
notes: Fall 2026: drop by Oct 4, 2026 for a 100% tuition refund; withdraw by Oct 18 for 50%; no refund after that (withdraw through Nov 13).

question: add drop deadline spring
notes: Spring 2027: last day to add online without dept. approval and to drop with a 100% refund is Sunday, Apr 4, 2027.

question: My schedule is a mess. Until when can I move classes around without a penalty?
notes: Adds and drops are done online in Beaver Hub by the add/drop deadlines in the Academic Calendar (end of week 1: Oct 4 for fall 2026). Week 2 adds need a department override.

question: I missed the deadline to get out of a class. What are my options now?
notes: After the drop deadline you withdraw: a W on the transcript, no GPA effect, partial or no refund per the calendar. Past the withdraw deadline, a Petition for Late Change of Registration ($20 fee, reviewed by the Academic Requirements Committee).

question: I'm an online student, do I get the same first week to switch classes around?
notes: Yes: through Sunday of the first week you may add or drop by web; in week 2 withdrawals are by web but adds go through Ecampus Student Services; after week 2 a late-change petition is required.

question: Can I pay my tuition in chunks instead of all at once?
notes: Yes: enroll in a payment plan at mybill.oregonstate.edu (Payment Plans tab), $15 enrollment fee; options differ by down payment and number of monthly payments.

question: i cant afford the whole bill right now, can i split it up monthly
notes: Payment plans: a down payment (25%-75% depending on the month you enroll) then 1-3 monthly payments; $15 fee; enroll through MyBill with ONID.

question: Does OSU do installments for tuition, and does it cost anything to sign up?
notes: Yes, payment plans for current students; $15.00 plan enrollment fee each time.

question: How much do I have to put down up front if I spread my bill across the term?
notes: Depends on the plan option / enrollment month: e.g. fall option A or C is 25% down then 3 monthly payments; E is 50% down; H (November) is 75% down then 1 payment.

question: Can my mom sign me up for the monthly tuition thing from her own login?
notes: Yes: students and their authorized users can enroll in payment plans through MyBill.

question: If I'm paying over time, do I still get hit with the late charge or blocked from signing up for classes?
notes: No: accounts in a current-term payment plan are exempt from that term's late fee ($85), and staying current lets you register even if the balance is over the registration threshold.

question: do online students get to pay in installments too
notes: Yes; Ask Ecampus points to Student Accounts' billing and payment pages (payment plans via MyBill, $15 fee).

question: Where can I get a tutor?
notes: The Academic Success Center's Academic Support page lists tutoring and college-based resources by subject (Vole Hole, Mole Hole, Pi Hole/MSLC, Supplemental Instruction, etc.); ASC is on the 3rd floor of the Valley Library.

question: im failing chem, is there somewhere on campus that helps for free
notes: The Mole Hole (Chemistry Support Center), 3rd floor of the Valley Library: tutoring for general, organic, physical chemistry and biochemistry by peer tutors and TAs. Also Supplemental Instruction study tables.

question: Who can help me with my calculus homework?
notes: Mathematics and Statistics Learning Center (MSLC), 108 Kidder Hall, for 200-300 level math; the Pi Hole (Valley Library 3rd floor) covers 100-level math (MTH 103/105/111/112).

question: Are there study groups for hard classes run by other students?
notes: Supplemental Instruction (SI) study tables: free, peer-led group study for specific courses; registration opens week 1, tables start week 2.

question: Is there someone who'll look over my essay before I turn it in?
notes: Writing Center: drop in at the Writing Studio (Valley Library main floor, Mon-Thu 10-6, Fri 10-4, no appointment) or submit a draft online for written feedback.

question: I need help with how to study in general, not one specific class. Who do I see?
notes: Academic Success Center: 45-minute academic coaching appointments (in person or Zoom), or drop in to talk with a Strategist on the 3rd floor of the Valley Library.

question: does osu have free homework help in the library
notes: Yes: the Valley Library hosts course support for chemistry, physics and 100-level math plus research and writing help; biology and other math support is nearby.

question: Is there peer help for engineering classes like statics?
notes: College of Engineering Peer Tutoring Program: free drop-in tutoring (in person and remote) by trained engineering students, for current engineering students.

question: I'm a distance student. Can I get a tutor online?
notes: Yes: Tutor.com live online tutoring, 30 free hours per academic term for enrolled Ecampus students, for Ecampus courses only.

question: How much are the meal plans?
notes: 2026-27 dining plans per term: Plan 1 $1,900, Plan 2 $1,600, Plan 3 $1,325, Plan 4 $1,050, Plan 5 $850 (Plan 5 for returning residents only).

question: what are the meal plan tiers and which one is cheapest
notes: Five plans; new students choose from Plans 1-4. Cheapest for new residents is Plan 4 ($1,050/term, $3,150/year); Plan 5 ($850/term) is only for returning on-campus residents.

question: Do I have to buy a meal plan if I live in the dorms?
notes: Yes: students living in the residence halls are required to have a dining plan, billed per term to the student account on top of the room rate.

question: Can I switch to a smaller food plan partway through the quarter?
notes: Only in the first three weeks of each term (larger or smaller, via 'Change Dining Plans' on the housing portal); after week 3 you can only move to a larger plan.

question: What happens to leftover meal money at the end of the year?
notes: Unspent Dining Dollars roll over automatically for continuing students and must be used within one year (they expire at the end of the following spring term).

question: How much is room and board for a year?
notes: 2026-27 most common estimate: Buxton double ($13,311) + Dining Plan 3 ($3,975) = $17,286; most affordable: economy triple + Plan 4 = $11,291.

question: Does my dining hall money work at the restaurants in the MU?
notes: Dining Dollars work at UHDS-run locations (including Off the Quad in the MU); MU Commons locations do not accept Dining Dollars, so use Orange Cash there (10% discount).

question: Is there a discount for paying with my meal plan?
notes: Residents get 15% off at dining-center micro-restaurants (Marketplace West, McNary, Southside Station at Arnold) and 10% at other UHDS locations and markets.

question: How do I switch majors?
notes: Meet with an advisor for the new major (set up a temporary connection in Beaver Hub if they are not on your Success Team); advising staff submit the online Change of Program request to the Registrar.

question: i want to move from engineering to business, who do i talk to
notes: An advisor in the college you want to move into; the Academic Advising page lists each college's steps for changing or adding a major.

question: Is there a deadline for a new major to count this term?
notes: Program change requests must be submitted (by advising staff) by 5:00 pm Friday of week 2 to be effective the current term; later requests take effect the next term.

question: How do I pick up a minor?
notes: Adding or dropping a minor needs advisor approval; the advisor submits it through the same Change of Program workflow to the Registrar.

question: I have no idea what I want to major in. Can I start undecided?
notes: Yes: the University Exploratory Studies Program (UESP) gives advising and career help while you explore; declare a college and major when you have decided.

question: I'm a master's student and want to move to a different program. How?
notes: Graduate students use the Change of Degree/Major/Certificate form, from the second term of enrollment up to the second-to-last term, at least one week before the term starts.

question: how do i change my major as an online student
notes: Contact Ecampus Student Services by email with your name, OSU ID number and the program you want to switch to.

question: Do I need to send SAT scores to get in?
notes: No: OSU is test-optional; scores, if submitted, are supplemental and never the sole reason for a decision.

question: When do I have to apply by for next fall?
notes: Fall 2027 first-year: Early Action Nov 2, 2026; priority deadline Feb 1, 2027 (Corvallis).

question: how much is the application fee and can i get it waived
notes: $65 undergraduate application fee; a fee waiver can be requested at the end of the application.

question: I got rejected. Can I ask them to take another look?
notes: Yes: applicants denied for academic reasons may petition the Undergraduate Admissions Committee for an exception.

question: What's the deposit to hold my spot once I'm accepted?
notes: The $200 Advance Tuition Deposit (ATD), credited toward the first term; Ecampus students are exempt.

question: Will my AP scores count for college credit?
notes: Yes: Admissions publishes the AP/IB score-to-credit tables; send scores to OSU (college code 4586).

question: How do I get counted as in-state for tuition?
notes: Only bona fide Oregon residents meeting the Residency Standards get resident tuition; the Residency Office in Admissions reviews status.

question: Where do I send my high school transcripts?
notes: Have the school send official transcripts electronically (e.g. Parchment, National Student Clearinghouse) or by mail in a sealed envelope to the Office of Admissions, 104 Kerr Administration Building.

question: How many college credits before I count as a transfer instead of a freshman?
notes: 24 transferable quarter credits (16 semester) after high school graduation; with fewer, high school work is also reviewed.

question: What English test score do I need if English isn't my first language?
notes: IELTS 6.5, Duolingo 110, or the TOEFL iBT minimums listed (80 with 16 per subsection if taken before Jan 21, 2026).

question: Can I work off campus on a student visa?
notes: F-1 students may work on campus up to 20 hours/week during the term; off-campus work needs authorization such as CPT or OPT through the Office of International Services.

question: I'm an international student flying home over break. What papers do I need to get back into the US?
notes: Original I-20 or DS-2019 with a valid travel signature, valid F-1/J-1 visa, passport valid 6+ months; request the travel signature in advance.

question: Can I come see the campus before I decide?
notes: Yes: campus tours and information sessions start at the Welcome Center in Reser Stadium; reserve a daily visit, or use the virtual tours.

question: The class I need is full. Can I get on a list for it?
notes: Yes, if the section has a waitlist (up to 3 courses). When a seat opens you get an email to your ONID address and have 24 hours to register.

question: How do I find out when I'm allowed to sign up for next term's classes?
notes: Beaver Hub > Academics > Check Your Registration Status; the window is based on class level and earned credits.

question: It says I have a hold and I can't sign up for classes. What do I do?
notes: Look up the hold on Holds @ OSU: each hold lists the office that placed it and the steps to lift it; view your holds in Beaver Hub.

question: Registration keeps kicking back a prerequisite error even though I took the class at community college
notes: Prerequisite/test score error: contact the department offering the course to check eligibility and request an override.

question: Can I sit in on a class without getting a grade?
notes: Yes, by audit: Audit Registration form with the instructor's permission during the second full week of the term; charged the same fees as credit; AUD on transcript.

question: How many credits can I take in one term before I need permission?
notes: Undergraduates can register for up to 19 credits when registration opens; overloads above the limits in the Academic Regulations need GPA/advisor approval, and 25+ credits needs a petition.

question: I failed a class. If I retake it does the F stop hurting my GPA?
notes: For a standard course the second attempt is the one that counts toward earned credit and GPA (AR 20), regardless of grade; the first stays on the transcript marked excluded.

question: Can I get extra time to finish a class after the term ends?
notes: Ask the instructor for an Incomplete (I) if you are passing and the reason is acceptable; the work must be resolved within one year or the alternate grade applies.

question: My evening group midterm overlaps with my work shift. Do I just lose the points?
notes: No: for group midterms an equivalent make-up exam must be provided to students who for good reason (schedule conflict, job, commute) cannot attend.

question: How do I get proof that I'm enrolled for my car insurance?
notes: Request a free enrollment verification through the National Student Clearinghouse (available after the term begins).

question: I need to take a year off. Do I have to reapply to come back?
notes: Not for a year: you become inactive only after four consecutive terms (not counting summer) without enrolling, then you apply for readmission; a longer planned leave can use PELP ($25).

question: Do I have to fill something out to graduate?
notes: Undergraduates do not apply: you are placed in the graduation pool near the end of your second-to-last term and the degree is awarded after requirements are met. Graduate students apply with their program.

question: How do I get the name I actually go by onto my class rosters?
notes: Set a name-in-use; it changes how your first name shows in Canvas, MyDegrees and advising systems. Legal name changes need the Biographical Information Update form plus documentation.

question: When are finals this fall?
notes: Fall 2026 finals week begins Monday, Dec 7, 2026 (classes end Dec 4).

question: Do we get the whole week off for Thanksgiving?
notes: No: Thanksgiving break is Thursday-Friday, Nov 26-27, 2026.

question: when can i start signing up for winter classes
notes: Winter 2027 priority registration begins Monday, Nov 16, 2026 (your own window depends on class standing).

question: When do fall grades come out?
notes: Fall 2026 grades are available online Wednesday, Dec 16, 2026.

question: What day is graduation this year?
notes: Commencement is Saturday, June 12, 2027 (Corvallis); OSU-Cascades is June 13.

question: When does school start next fall?
notes: Fall 2027 classes begin Wednesday, Sept 22, 2027 (4-year calendar).

question: Is there class on Veterans Day?
notes: No: Veterans Day is an observed university holiday, Wednesday Nov 11, 2026.

question: How do I check what classes I still need for my degree?
notes: MyDegrees (Beaver Hub > Academics > MyDegrees): an online degree audit checklist; the Planner lets you map future terms.

question: What's the difference between a double major and getting two degrees?
notes: A double degree needs at least 32 credits beyond the minimum for one degree and each degree is recorded separately; a dual major is one degree with two majors.

question: What gen eds do I have to take?
notes: Core Education (OSU's general education): a Foundational Core and a Signature Core, required for undergraduates starting summer 2025 or later; earlier students follow the Bacc Core.

question: How many credits until I'm a sophomore?
notes: 45 earned credits = sophomore, 90 = junior, 135 = senior (Academic Regulations).

question: What GPA do I need to make the dean's list?
notes: OSU's term Honor Roll: at least 6 graded undergraduate credits with a 3.5 or higher term GPA (AR 21).

question: What's a WIC class and do I have to take one?
notes: Writing Intensive Curriculum: a major-specific upper-division writing course; each student completes the WIC course for their own major.

question: Do I have to take a math placement test before I can register for math?
notes: Yes: all students in New Student Onboarding take the ALEKS placement assessment; the score can only improve placement if you already have college math credit.

question: How do I get into the honors college?
notes: Complete the Honors College application (the HC section of the OSU application, or the separate HC application for current students), including short-answer questions.

question: How do I get involved in research as an undergrad?
notes: The Undergraduate Research office: research is open to students in every discipline; its site explains how to find mentors and opportunities.

question: What is a microcredential, is it like a minor?
notes: Smaller than a minor: a focused set of at least three courses, usually 8-12 credits, awarded as a digital badge.

question: what does a B+ count as for gpa
notes: B+ = 3.3 grade points per credit (A 4.0, A- 3.7, B 3.0).

question: What happens if my GPA drops below a 2.0?
notes: A term GPA below 2.0 puts you on Academic Warning; a cumulative OSU GPA below 2.0 after 24+ attempted credits is Academic Probation; a further term below 2.0 while on probation leads to Academic Suspension (AR 22).

question: When is my bill due and what happens if I pay late?
notes: Fall 2026 bills are due Nov 1 (statement emailed Oct 5); an $85 late fee applies once per term to balances over $500 after the due date.

question: I need money fast for rent this week. Does OSU do short-term loans?
notes: Emergency loans up to $350, one per term, for degree-seeking students enrolled at least half-time with no financial holds; check eligibility in Beaver Hub.

question: Where do I get the tax form for the tuition I paid?
notes: The 1098-T is mailed in January and can be viewed online in Beaver Hub.

question: If I go part time will I lose my financial aid?
notes: Aid is packaged for full-time (12+ credits undergrad) and adjusted to your enrollment on the Census Date; some aid is prorated or lost below full or half time.

question: When does my financial aid money actually show up?
notes: Aid is disbursed onto the student billing account about a week before each term starts, in three equal installments (fall, winter, spring).

question: My dad lost his job after we filed the FAFSA. Can my aid be recalculated?
notes: Yes: submit a Special Conditions Appeal for a major change in finances outside your control; it can recalculate Pell Grant and subsidized loan eligibility.

question: What grades do I need to keep getting financial aid?
notes: Satisfactory Academic Progress: 2.0 OSU GPA for undergraduates, complete at least 67% of attempted credits, and finish within the maximum time frame.

question: I had a family emergency and had to leave mid-term. Any chance of getting tuition back?
notes: Submit a Tuition Refund Appeal to the Tuition Appeal Committee for unexpected, serious circumstances; aid may have to be returned after a full withdrawal.

question: Can I change dorm rooms if I don't get along with my roommate?
notes: Yes: room changes and swaps are available weeks 2-9 in fall and winter (2-6 in spring) if space allows; talk to your RA first about roommate conflicts.

question: What day do we move into the dorms?
notes: Fall 2026 move-in is Wed-Fri, Sept 16-18, on an assigned date by hall; time slots are picked in late August.

question: Do I have to pay for laundry in the dorms?
notes: No: laundry is free for campus residents (no coins or cards); bring your own detergent.

question: Is the gym free for students?
notes: Yes for Corvallis students: Rec Sports (Dixon) membership comes with the student incidental fee.

question: I got a parking ticket. How do I fight it?
notes: File an appeal online with Transportation Services within the appeal window; unpaid balances over 30 days may go to collections.

question: Is the bus free?
notes: Yes: the Beaver Bus campus shuttle is free, and Corvallis Transit System is fare-free citywide.

question: I lost my student ID. How do I get a new one?
notes: Suspend the card in MyCard, then get a replacement at the ID Center with photo ID; $30.

question: Is therapy free for students?
notes: Yes for Corvallis students: CAPS counseling is fully covered by student fees.

question: Is what I tell a campus therapist kept private from my parents and professors?
notes: Yes: CAPS conversations are confidential under state and federal law, with rare safety and legal exceptions.

question: I'm sick. How do I see a doctor on campus?
notes: Book through the Patient Portal or call 541-737-9355; Health Center (by Reser Stadium) or Rapid Care @ Tebeau for same-day acute care.

question: Can I get a doctor's note for missing class?
notes: No: Student Health Services does not provide written excuses for missed classes or exams.

question: Does the health center take my parents' insurance?
notes: SHS is in-network with most major insurers and bills them (except out-of-state Medicaid).

question: I don't have health insurance. Can I buy it through school?
notes: Yes: the OSU Student Health Insurance Plan (SHIP) for domestic students; international students are enrolled automatically.

question: where can i get tested for STDs
notes: Student Health Services does STI testing; DamTested at-home kits can be picked up at the Wellness Kiosk or Health Center Lab.

question: Where can I pick up a prescription near campus?
notes: The Samaritan Pharmacy in the Samaritan Athletic Medicine Center across from Reser Stadium; other Corvallis pharmacies are listed.

question: It's 2am and I'm really stressed, not an emergency. Is there anyone to talk to?
notes: Anytime Anywhere (TELUS Health): free 24/7 counselor by app or phone; or call CAPS at 541-737-2131 option 1 after hours; 988 for crisis.

question: I was assaulted and I'm not sure I want to report it. Who can I talk to privately?
notes: CAPE survivor advocates (confidential; 24/7 line 541-737-2030) explain options without requiring a report; CAPS Interpersonal Violence Services offers confidential counseling.

question: Can someone help me find a long-term therapist off campus?
notes: Thriving Campus: a searchable directory of local providers filtered by specialty, insurance and identity.

question: I have ADHD. Can I get extra time on tests?
notes: Apply to Disability Access Services with documentation; extended time and reduced-distraction testing are approved individually and apply to timed in-person tests.

question: What paperwork do I need to prove my disability?
notes: Documentation from a qualified healthcare, educational or other professional describing the disability and its impact; DAS may ask for more.

question: I broke my wrist and can't write. Is there any help for finals?
notes: Contact DAS for temporary-injury accommodations as soon as possible, with documentation of the injury, and talk with your instructors.

question: Can I get someone to take notes for me in lecture?
notes: DAS notetaking accommodation: notetaking technology first (e.g. audio-note software, smartpen); peer notetakers or real-time transcribing depending on the disability's impact.

question: Can my emotional support dog live with me in the dorm?
notes: ESAs are a housing accommodation requested through DAS (not the same as service animals, which may go anywhere open to the public).

question: My condition flares up and I miss class sometimes. Can I get leeway on attendance?
notes: DAS may approve Flexibility with Attendance/Assignments for chronic conditions with periodic flare-ups; reasonable flexibility, not unlimited.

question: I need a room to myself for medical reasons. How do I ask?
notes: Request a housing accommodation through DAS; UHDS implements it. UHDS housing deadlines still apply.

question: Can I take fewer classes and still count as full time because of my disability?
notes: Yes: with the Reduced Credit Load accommodation, as few as 6 credits per term can count as full-time; check effects with Financial Aid.

question: How do I get my textbooks in audio or large print?
notes: DAS Accessible Formats: course materials converted to e-text, large print, Braille, accessible PDF, etc.

question: They turned down my accommodation request. Can I fight it?
notes: Talk with your DAS adviser first, then appeal in writing; without new documentation, appeal within 5 days of the denial.

question: Where can I park with a handicap placard?
notes: With a DMV ADA placard you may use any ADA space on campus (350+), but an OSU parking permit is still required.

question: Where can I print something on campus?
notes: Valley Library: print from library computers or your laptop to BeaverPrint and release the job at any printer with your OSU ID.

question: I can't afford my textbooks. Is there any way to borrow them?
notes: Basic Needs Center Textbook Lending Program (free term-long loans) and library Course Reserves.

question: How do I find an internship?
notes: Career Development Center: search Handshake (log in with ONID email), attend career fairs, or meet a career advisor.

question: I'm a student with a toddler. Is there help paying for daycare?
notes: Family Resource Center: OSU Student Child Care Assistance for Corvallis students paying for child care (fall 2026 applications due Oct 9), plus campus child care options.

question: I'm in the hospital and going to miss a bunch of class. Who lets my professors know?
notes: Student Care helps students through hospitalization, illness and crises; when you cannot contact instructors yourself, the Office of the Dean of Students can send an Emergency Notification to your faculty and advisor. OSU has no excused-absence policy.

question: How do I use my GI Bill here?
notes: Apply at va.gov for a Certificate of Eligibility; Military & Veteran Resources explains each benefit chapter and the Registrar's VA team certifies enrollment.

question: Can I use ChatGPT on my homework?
notes: Only as your instructor allows: faculty set course-specific GenAI expectations (check the syllabus); using it without authorization counts as cheating under academic integrity rules.

question: Will a cheating write-up stay on my record forever?
notes: Disciplinary records are sealed automatically seven years after the case closes; students may request early sealing.

question: How do I report a professor for treating me unfairly because of my race?
notes: Report discrimination or discriminatory harassment to Equal Opportunity & Access using its online report form.

question: I think my club is hazing new members. What should I do?
notes: Use the Report Hazing form from Student Community Standards; the page defines hazing and the reporting options.

question: Someone made a racist comment in my residence hall. Where do I report that?
notes: Report it to the Bias Response Team (Office of Institutional Diversity) or request a consultation; the page gives email/phone while the online form is unavailable.

question: How do I keep my name and address out of the student directory?
notes: Limit your Directory Profile in MyOregonState, or request confidential status with the Registrar so no directory information is released.

question: Are we allowed to protest on campus, and can we chalk the sidewalks?
notes: Assembly and protest are protected expression subject to content-neutral time, place and manner rules; chalking and posting on building exteriors and fixtures is restricted.

question: I got called for jury duty in the middle of the term
notes: Talk with your instructors and advisor; you may ask the court to defer, and faculty should not penalize verified jury service.

question: I'm pregnant. Do my professors have to work with me on deadlines?
notes: Yes: reasonable modifications for pregnancy and related conditions are provided individually; contact Equal Opportunity & Access.

question: My landlord won't give back my deposit. Is there a free lawyer for students?
notes: ASOSU Student Legal Services gives legal advice and representation for off-campus issues such as landlord-tenant disputes. (The office's own site is not stored; these pages describe it.)

question: How do I get on the wifi?
notes: Students connect to eduroam or OSU_Secure with ONID credentials; free.

question: My parents are visiting. Is there guest internet they can use?
notes: Yes: the Visitor network; connect, open a browser and accept the terms (free, up to four hours per session).

question: I got a new phone and now I can't get past the two-step login
notes: Reactivate Duo Mobile on the new phone (keep the old phone active until the new one works); if locked out, contact the Service Desk.

question: Who do I call when my laptop won't connect to anything?
notes: The UIT Service Desk: submit a help request or call; college help desks are also listed.

question: Can I get MATLAB for free?
notes: Yes: OSU's site license covers students on up to 4 personally owned devices at no charge.

question: Is Photoshop free for students?
notes: No: OSU's Creative Cloud license is for faculty and staff; students needing it on a personal device buy it from Adobe at the student discount.

question: Do I need a VPN to get to school stuff from home?
notes: OSU's VPN is free for students for a secure connection to the campus network; most library resources work off campus through the library proxy with ONID and Duo.

question: Is there an OSU app for my phone?
notes: The OSU Mobile app was retired Jan 1, 2026; use Beaver Hub and the Campus Map on the web.

question: where do i log in to see my assignments and grades for my classes
notes: Canvas, OSU's learning management system (course materials, assignments, grades).

question: Where do I check my school email?
notes: Outlook (Exchange Online) is OSU's official email; sign in with your OSU account.

question: Does OSU give students an AI chatbot?
notes: Yes: enrolled students get the data-protected version of Microsoft Copilot by signing in with OSU credentials.

question: Can I set up my own router in my dorm room?
notes: No: personal wireless routers and access points are not allowed in the halls; bring an Ethernet cable for the wired port.

question: I live in Texas and take everything online. Do I pay out-of-state rates?
notes: No: Ecampus courses cost the same for residents, nonresidents and international students ($409/credit for most undergraduate programs in 2026-27).

question: Are online classes go-at-your-own-speed?
notes: No: Ecampus courses follow the same 11-week term with instructor deadlines; you can log in any time of day.

question: I'm on campus but want to take one class online. Do I have to switch programs?
notes: No: any OSU student can take Ecampus courses, though Ecampus students get earlier registration access to them.

question: Do I need a webcam for tests in online classes?
notes: If the course requires proctored exams, online proctoring uses a webcam, microphone and screen share; the syllabus says whether proctoring is required.

question: Is there a coach or mentor for online students who feel lost?
notes: Yes: Ecampus success navigators offer one-on-one success coaching; schedule an appointment online.

question: Can online students walk at graduation in Corvallis?
notes: Yes: Ecampus graduates are invited to the in-person commencement (June 12, 2027) and an Ecampus reception that morning.

question: How do distance students get books from the library?
notes: OSU Libraries mails books to your home address with free delivery and return shipping; articles come by Scan & Deliver or Interlibrary Loan.

question: I'm an online student and got hit with a surprise expense. Is there any emergency money?
notes: The Ecampus Financial Hardship Grant for online undergraduate degree-seeking students with an unexpected emergency; requires a FAFSA or ORSAA on file.

question: Can online students who live out of state use the campus counseling center?
notes: CAPS can only counsel students located in Oregon, but all students (including Ecampus) get free 24/7 support through Anytime Anywhere, plus help finding a local counselor.

question: What's on the menu at McNary tonight?
notes: Not in data: daily menus are live data on the dining menu system; the Food @ OSU menus page is stored empty.
